topic: Upper Ontologies (BFO, SUMO, DOLCE, GFO) - September 2026 Research Update

findings.title: BFO 2.0 and ISO/IEC 21838-2:2021 Standard — Current Status
findings.key_findings: BFO 2.0 was released as an ISO/IEC 21838-2:2021 standard, establishing BFO as the first ISO-standardized top-level ontology. The BFO 2.0 OWL version (current at purl.obolibrary.org/obo/bfo.owl) is a classes-only specification with 36 classes, 40 object properties, and 602 axioms. Core relations incorporation was postponed to BFO 2.1 (experimental version available). BFO 2.0 is not strictly backward compatible with BFO 1.1; automated conversion tools exist at bfoconvert.hegroup.org. The BFO 2.0 CLIF (first-order logic) version is implemented on OntoHub. Used by 130+ ontology projects worldwide and 700+ open-source ontologies. The ISO/IEC 21838 multi-part standard includes Part 1 (requirements for top-level ontologies) and Part 2 (BFO specification).

findings.title: DOLCE OWL Approximation: Modular Approach with DOLCEbasicOWL and DOLCEnaryRelOWL
findings.key_findings: Porello et al. propose a novel modular approach to OWL rendering of DOLCE, addressing the limited expressivity of OWL 2 compared to DOLCE's original first-order modal logic (D18) and Common Logic (DOLCEsimpleFOL) versions. Two core modules: (1) DOLCEbasicOWL — main taxonomy and binary relations; (2) DOLCEnaryRelOWL — extension for n-ary relations (n>2), including temporalized relations (temporary parthood, constitution, participation) and mereological relations (binary sum). Key innovation: automated proof that DOLCEsimpleFOL entails the OWL 2 modules (using Prover9), ensuring compatibility with the original theory. The modular design enables domain ontologies to link to core modules and verify consistency. DOLCE is also an ISO standard (ISO/IEC 21838). Previous OWL versions (DOLCE-Lite, DOLCE-Ultralite) did not prove entailment from the FOL version.

findings.title: SUMO — Current Status and Usage (2025-2026)
findings.venue: GitHub (ontologyportal/sumo), ontolearner benchmarking, IEEE Standard Upper Ontology effort
findings.key_findings: SUMO remains actively maintained by Articulate Software (originally Teknowledge). It contains ~4,525 classes, 80,034 individuals, 587 properties (per ontolearner metrics). SUMO is expressed in SUO-KIF (higher-order logic, LISP-like syntax) and TPTP formats, with mappings to WordNet. It includes a mid-level ontology (MILO) and dozens of domain ontologies. Used for semantic interoperability, information extraction, document retrieval, NLP. Recent research extends SUMO into computer vision, offline RL, and LLM optimization. The Sigma knowledge engineering environment provides open-source tooling. SUMO was the 'starter document' for the IEEE Standard Upper Ontology effort. Still considered relatively mature but not actively expanding at the upper level.

findings.title: Industrial Ontologies Foundry (IOF) — 2025-2026 Major Releases
findings.venue: OAGi / IOF GitHub (iofoundry/ontology), OAGi Press Release
findings.key_findings: IOF Core Ontology uses BFO as its upper-level framework. Major 202502 release (Dec 2025) introduced flexible IRI architecture, normalized prefixes, migration tooling, and three new provisional modules: Certification, Production Planning, Product-Service Systems (PSS). 202601 release (Mar 2026) added Consumable/ConsumableRole, new material composition properties (isMadeOfAtSomeTime, isMadeOfAtAllTime), InputSpecificationPattern with FOL axioms, Certificate module, and provisional Production Planning capability.rdf. 202602 release (May 2026) migrated BMIC terms to Supply Chain, added Recipe Process/Procedural Classification Utilities. BMIC biopharma ontologies to be merged into IOF suite in Q1 2026. IOF supports digital twins, smart manufacturing, supply chain optimization, industrial automation. 164 stars, 36 forks on GitHub.

findings.title: OBO Foundry — 2025-2026 Infrastructure and Community Updates
findings.venue: OBO Foundry Newsletter Issue 10 (April 2026), OBO Dashboard
findings.key_findings: OBO Foundry continues to rely on BFO as its upper-level ontology (700+ BFO-based ontologies). Dashboard updated March 2026; infrastructure migrated from Oracle to PostgreSQL, containerized via Kubernetes, redesigned responsive web interfaces. Standardization Guidelines document finalized (technical, content, release, communication considerations). Principle 3 strengthened: ontology PURLs must resolve to OWL files; term PURLs to term-centric pages. New ontologies accepted: Physiologically Based Pharmacokinetics Ontology (PBPKO). Under review: Intrinsically Disordered Proteins, Precision Fermentation, Clinical Metadata Exploration. AI integration advancing: OBO Academy sessions on Claude Code for ontology development (2025-2026), AI4Curation guidance resources, dedicated Slack channels (#ethical-ai, #ai). Ontology of Adverse Events (OAE) expanded to 10,829 terms (251% increase since 2014).

findings.title: Comparison Studies: BFO, DOLCE, GFO, SUMO Alignment and Matching
findings.venue: CEUR Workshop Proceedings Vol-2519 (OAEI 2018 evaluation), Applied Ontology, JOWO 2025 (FOUST workshop)
findings.key_findings: Automatic matching systems (OAEI 2018) evaluated on BFO, DOLCE, GFO, SUMO alignments. Best F-measure for BFO-GFO pair (6/11 correspondences lexically close, e.g., bfo:SpatialRegion / gfo:SpatialRegion). BFO-DOLCE alignment shows consistent recall across matchers. ROMULUS library provides reference alignments for BFO-DOLCE-GFO. Manual alignments exist: BFO 1.0-DOLCE (Temal et al. 2010), DOLCE-SUMO (Oberle et al. 2007). JOWO 2025 FOUST workshop (Sep 2025) included papers on mereology of slots, definitional ontology construction, BFO design patterns vs information exchange standards, and SULO (simplified upper-level ontology by Dumontier et al.). Khan & Keet (2013) found substantially fewer automatic alignments than manual for BFO-DOLCE-GFO.

findings.title: Realism vs Nominalism in Upper Ontology Design — Philosophical Foundations
findings.venue: Applied Ontology, FOIS proceedings, Onto-Med GFO documentation, PMC literature
findings.key_findings: BFO explicitly adopts a **realist** approach: classes denote entities existing objectively in reality; definitions adhere to strict criteria for reusability. BFO's continuant/occurant dichotomy reflects a realist view of temporal persistence. DOLCE takes a **descriptive/cognitive** approach: captures categories underlying natural language and human commonsense (not necessarily mind-independent reality). GFO explicitly provides **openness regarding philosophical positions** — offers categories as universals, concepts, or symbolic structures, accommodating realism, conceptualism, and nominalism. GFO's 'persistants' category coherently integrates objects and processes without committing to one metaphysical stance. Literature notes realism-based ontology design is challenging: BFO's upper level is well-worked (35 classes, depth 5), but shortage of mid-level realism-based resources. The PMC article 'Problems of Realism-Based Ontology Design' (diabetes camps case study) highlights training demands. SUMO includes both particulars and universals. The JOWO 2025 POWER workshop addressed 'realizable entities' bridging dispositions and plans.

findings.title: Upper Ontology Applications in Industry — Manufacturing, Digital Twins, Biopharma
findings.venue: JOWO 2025 FOMI Workshop, Expert Systems with Applications (2025), OAGi/IOF releases
findings.key_findings: BFO is the most preferred upper ontology in manufacturing (per 2024 review). IOF uses BFO as foundational layer for digital twins, smart manufacturing, supply chain optimization, industrial automation. JOWO 2025 FOMI workshop (Sep 2025) papers: SysDO for cross-domain aircraft manufacturing; ontology for inorganic material analytical methods; ontology design pattern for industry classification (FIO); ontological validation of simulation models; precedence matrices from CAD files. I40GO (Industry 4.0 Global Ontology, 2025) cites MASON upper ontology for manufacturing systems. OAGi/IOF adding Certification, Production Planning, Product-Service System modules for Industry 4.0. BMIC biopharma ontologies merging into IOF Q1 2026. OBO biomedical ontologies (OAE, GO, FMA, CL) built on BFO enable pharmacovigilance, precision medicine, cross-disciplinary analysis. gistBFO (Semantic Arts) provides business-focused BFO-compatible upper ontology used in 100+ commercial implementations (finance, government, pharma).

findings.title: GFO (General Formal Ontology) — Modular Architecture and 2020-2025 Developments
findings.venue: Onto-Med Research Group (Leipzig), GitHub (Onto-Med/GFO), Applied Ontology 2022
findings.key_findings: GFO developed by Onto-Med (Herre, Heller, Loebe, Burek) since 1999. Key features: coherent integration of objects/processes via 'persistants'; time/space as sui generis entities with 'coincidence' relation; situoids as comprehensible wholes; elaborate functions/roles; philosophical openness (universals, concepts, symbolic structures). Modular architecture: gfo-base.owl core module with separate namespaced extensions (time, space, processes) — not all mutually consistent. GFO-light provides simplified view for domain ontology foundations. 2022 Applied Ontology paper (Loebe, Burek, Herre) is latest comprehensive publication. 2020 FOIS paper 'Towards GFO 2.0: Architecture, Modules and Applications'. 2023 function modeling patterns. OWL versions available at w3id.org/gfo with versioned IRIs. Native formalization is FOL (partial axiomatizations in drafts).

findings.title: DOLCE in ISO/IEC 21838 and DOLCEsimpleFOL
findings.venue: ISO/IEC 21838 standard, Applied Ontology 2025, COLORE repository
findings.key_findings: DOLCE is standardized in ISO/IEC 21838 (alongside BFO). DOLCE originated in QS5 modal logic (D18 version, 2003). DOLCEsimpleFOL is a first-order logic version in Common Logic (CLIF, TPTP, Prover9) created for ISO 21838 inclusion. Modular consistency proof via Hets/Kutz-Mossakowski (2011). The DOLCEsimpleFOL version enables automated theorem proving and model finding (Mace4). Available at LOA CNR and COLORE repository (github.com/gruninger/colore). DOLCE-Ultralite (DUL) remains widely used OWL version but lacks formal entailment proof from FOL version. The 2025 Porello et al. paper builds on the ISO-targeted OWL version to create DOLCEbasicOWL and DOLCEnaryRelOWL with formal compatibility proof.

findings.title: SULO — Simplified Upper-Level Ontology (JOWO 2025 FOUST)
findings.key_findings: SULO (Simplified Upper-Level Ontology) presented by Dumontier, Çelebi, Gilani, et al. at FOUST workshop. Aims to provide a minimal, accessible upper ontology bridging foundational ontologies. Related to POWER workshop on 'realizable entities' (dispositions, plans) extending BFO. Indicates ongoing community interest in simplified/pragmatic upper ontologies alongside comprehensive ones like BFO, DOLCE, GFO, SUMO.

findings.title: Ontology Alignment Evaluation Initiative (OAEI) 2018 Results on Foundational Ontologies
findings.key_findings: Schmidt, Trojahn, Vieira evaluated OAEI 2018 matching systems on foundational ontology pairs: BFO-DOLCE, BFO-GFO, DOLCE-GFO, DOLCE-SUMO. Reference alignments from ROMULUS (BFO-DOLCE-GFO) and Oberle et al. 2007 (DOLCE-SUMO). Results: automatic matchers still substantially underperform manual alignment. Best results for BFO-GFO (lexical similarity). All matchers report same recall for BFO-DOLCE-Lite. Challenges: rich axiomatization, philosophical differences, limited lexical overlap. Confirms Khan & Keet (2013) findings — limited progress in automated foundational ontology matching.

summary: As of September 2026, the upper ontology landscape shows: (1) BFO 2.0 is the only ISO-standardized upper ontology (ISO/IEC 21838-2:2021), widely adopted in biomedicine (OBO Foundry, 700+ ontologies) and industry (IOF, 130+ projects); BFO 2.1 with relations is in development. (2) DOLCE has advanced a modular OWL approximation (DOLCEbasicOWL + DOLCEnaryRelOWL) with formal compatibility proofs to its FOL version (DOLCEsimpleFOL), also ISO-standardized. (3) SUMO remains stable with mid-level MILO and domain ontologies, used for NLP and semantic interoperability, with recent ML integrations. (4) IOF is the major industrial adoption, releasing 3 major versions in 2025-2026 with new modules for Certification, Production Planning, PSS, and biopharma integration — all built on BFO. (5) OBO Foundry continues expanding (10,829 terms in OAE) with infrastructure modernization and AI-assisted curation. (6) Comparison studies confirm persistent alignment challenges; BFO-GFO shows best automated matching; manual alignments still superior. (7) Philosophical diversity persists: BFO (realist), DOLCE (descriptive/cognitive), GFO (pluralistic/neutral), SUMO (universals+particulars). (8) Industry applications accelerating: digital twins, Industry 4.0, biopharma, supply chain, aircraft manufacturing — with BFO as dominant upper-level choice.
